_comment: TEMPLATE, not a ready graph. setup-tavus.mjs expands this into a FULL 8-panel chain (4 nodes per panel + 1 lead-in + up to 4 prefill nodes + 1 terminal = up to 38 nodes) every time, regardless of difficulty. Difficulty (0/2/4) is a runtime choice told to the PAL via conversational_context, not a build-time shape — the lead-in node below branches to the right entry point based on that context. Panels before the entry point simply go unreached for that session; the graph still has to define them because it is provisioned once and difficulty varies per session. The graph MUST stay acyclic: Tavus accepts a cyclic graph at POST /v2/objectives and returns 200, but every conversation using it dies ~1s after startup with exception_encountered_during_conversation_startup (verified 2026-07-27, see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md T1 finding 2, decision D16). Do not add allow_loops or an edge back to an earlier panel. Rewritten 2026-07-29 per docs.tavus.io/sections/onboarding-guide/objectives (one objective per distinct outcome, name tool calls explicitly, keep the PAL system prompt from conflicting with the objectives) to fix panels not reliably logging: every step now explicitly names log_zine_page / log_understanding_check / canvas_clear, and the test/retest/reexplain steps explicitly choose a canvas.question Magic Canvas card for discrete-option questions vs. an explicit spoken instruction to answer on Excalidraw and click Send for open-ended ones. Prefill (0/2/4 worked-example panels) was originally ONE objective asking the model to silently self-loop 'panel_number 1 through the difficulty count' in a single turn — observed live to stall partway (e.g. 3 of 4 panels logged, then nothing) with no structural checkpoint to catch it. Decomposed 2026-07-29 into explicit prefillChain nodes, one per prefilled panel, same one-objective-per-outcome fix already applied to the main loop.

leadIn.objective_prompt: The session context already provides the concept and difficulty level (0, 2, or 4) — never ask the student for either. If the difficulty is 0, skip prefill entirely: say one brief sentence transitioning into the first panel, then move on to it. If the difficulty is 2 or 4, say ONE brief sentence that you're pulling together a few worked examples — say this only once, never repeat it — then proceed silently into the prefill step; do not narrate, summarize, or announce it again.

conditional.prefill_panel_1: the session context states the difficulty level is 2, or states the difficulty level is 4
conditional.panel_1_await: the session context states the difficulty level is 0, or does not state a difficulty level at all

prefillChain.objective_prompt: Silently call the log_zine_page tool once for panel_number 1, source "prefill", with a distinct, real worked example grounded in the attached course material — never a placeholder. Never speak or write the words "log_zine_page", its arguments, or any JSON, and never narrate or summarize this panel's content aloud.

Silently call the log_zine_page tool once for panel_number 2, source "prefill", with a distinct, real worked example grounded in the attached course material — never a placeholder or a repeat of panel 1. Never speak, narrate, or summarize this aloud.

next_conditional_objectives.panel_3_await: the session context states the difficulty level is 2
next_conditional_objectives.prefill_panel_3: the session context states the difficulty level is 4

prefillChain.objective_prompt: Silently call the log_zine_page tool once for panel_number 3, source "prefill", with a distinct, real worked example grounded in the attached course material — never a placeholder or a repeat of an earlier panel. Never speak, narrate, or summarize this aloud.

Silently call the log_zine_page tool once for panel_number 4, source "prefill", with a distinct, real worked example grounded in the attached course material — never a placeholder or a repeat of an earlier panel. Never speak, narrate, or summarize this aloud. Once logged, prefill is complete — move on to the interactive panels.

panelChain.objective_prompt: Invite the student to write or sketch their own understanding of panel {N} on the Excalidraw canvas. Wait for their notes — they arrive as spoken text. Once received, move to testing.

Test understanding with a TRANSFER question: pose one small new problem and ask whether and how their concept applies to it. Never ask them to "explain it back". If the question has discrete answer options, render it as a canvas.question Magic Canvas card. If it is open-ended, ask it aloud AND explicitly tell the student to write or sketch their answer on the Excalidraw canvas, then click "Send notes to Professor Riso" so you receive it — never wait silently for an Excalidraw answer without saying this out loud. Judge the response solid, shaky, or confused, and call log_understanding_check for panel {N}, attempt 1.

Re-explain panel {N} more simply, from a different angle. Ask the student to answer once more — either revise their notes or answer a new small problem — using the same rule as before: a canvas.question Magic Canvas card for a question with discrete options, or the Excalidraw canvas plus an explicit spoken instruction to click "Send notes to Professor Riso" for an open-ended one. This is the only re-explanation for this panel. If a slide from the course material would help make this concrete, this is the moment to bring it up.

Test the student's revised understanding with one more small TRANSFER question — different from attempt 1, still never "explain it back", still following the canvas.question-card-or-Excalidraw-and-Send rule. Judge the response solid, shaky, or confused, and call log_understanding_check for panel {N}, attempt 2. There is no third attempt regardless of the result.

conditional.gentle_correct: understanding is still shaky or confused after the re-explanation

panelChain.objective_prompt: The student is still confused after one re-explanation and there is no third attempt. Gently tell them the correct understanding of panel {N} in a sentence or two — no dwelling on the miss, warm and direct. A relevant slide here can make the correct explanation concrete instead of just spoken. Then write the panel yourself in clear, correct language and call log_zine_page with panel_number {N}, source "prefill" — this is your explanation, not the student's, so it must never be logged as source "student". If a canvas.question card is currently shown for this panel, immediately call canvas_clear so it disappears. Then move on.

Agree on a light-polish version of the student's own words for panel {N} — recognisably theirs, not your paraphrase — and call log_zine_page with panel_number {N} and source "student". If a canvas.question card is currently shown for this panel, immediately call canvas_clear so it disappears. Then move on.

terminal.objective_prompt: The zine is complete. Give a short recap naming what the student proved and where they fought hardest, for example 'base cases — first try; recursion took two rounds, that's the normal hard part'. Then let them know they can export their zine.
